# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `rhiza docs` from the command registry. Do not edit. -->

Every command takes the global flags, prints markdown or, with `--json`, JSON, and exits with one of the codes below.

## Global flags

- `--json`: Print JSON instead of markdown
- `--dry-run`: Build a write and print it; write nothing
- `--change <ref>`: The change set to act on (env RHIZA_CHANGE)
- `--actor <ref>`: Who performs the call (env RHIZA_ACTOR)
- `--for <ref>`: Whom the call acts for (env RHIZA_FOR)
- `--record`: Write in a record change set landed in one step
- `-h, --help`: Show this help, or describe a command

## Exit codes

- `0`: Success
- `1`: Any other error
- `2`: Usage error: unknown command or flag, a missing or bad argument
- `3`: Conflict: the state changed or does not allow the call
- `4`: Not found: the named node, change set, run or operation does not exist

## rhiza accept

Accept a proposed change set.

```
rhiza accept [--rule <rule>] [--reason <reason>]
```

Appends to the log.

Arguments and flags:

- `--rule`: The rule the decision is made under; default owner
- `--reason`: Why

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_set` (string): The change set moved
- `cleared_current` (boolean): True if the move ended the current change set and cleared it
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `entry` (string): The entry written; absent in a dry run
- `from` (string): The state before the move
- `reason` (string): The reason of an accept or reject
- `rule` (string): The rule of an accept or reject
- `to` (string): The state after the move

## rhiza add

Add a node.

```
rhiza add <kind> <handle> [--parent <parent>] [--before <before>] [--after <after>] [--field <field>]... [--json-field <json-field>]...
```

Appends to the log.

Arguments and flags:

- `<kind>`: The node's kind (required; one of intent, capability, constraint, decision, question, evidence, source, actor, anchor, note)
- `<handle>`: The node's handle: lower-case words joined by single dashes, unique among live nodes (required)
- `--parent`: The parent node (capabilities and intents only, same kind); default a root
- `--before`: Place it just before this sibling
- `--after`: Place it just after this sibling; default after the last one
- `--field`: A text field, name=text (repeatable)
- `--json-field`: A JSON field, name=<json> (repeatable)

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_set` (string): The change set written to (with --record, the new record change set)
- `drop` (array of string): Dry run only: the op IDs the entry would drop
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `entry` (string): The ops entry written; absent in a dry run
- `links` (array of string): The links the write created or retired, sorted
- `nodes` (array of string): The nodes the write created or changed, sorted; link endpoints are not included
- `ops` (array): Dry run only: the ops the entry would carry, as canonical op JSON
- `record` (boolean): True if the write opened and landed a record change set

## rhiza anchor refresh

Re-fingerprint an anchor from the working tree into the current change set.

```
rhiza anchor refresh <anchor>
```

Appends to the log.

Arguments and flags:

- `<anchor>`: The anchor: an ID, a unique ID prefix of 4+ characters, or a live node's handle (required)

Output (`--json` fields):

- `anchor` (string): The anchor
- `change_set` (string): The change set written to; absent when unchanged
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `entry` (string): The ops entry written; absent when unchanged and in a dry run
- `fingerprint` (string): The fingerprint of the working tree
- `previous` (string): The fingerprint the anchor held; absent if it had none
- `unchanged` (boolean): True if the fingerprint already matched the working tree, so nothing was written

## rhiza apply

Apply many writes as one entry: a JSON file {"writes":[{"op":"add",...},...]} whose items are add, set, mv, retire, link or unlink requests plus "op".

```
rhiza apply <file>
```

Appends to the log.

Input: {"writes":[...]}, at least one item; each item is one of add | set | mv | retire | link | unlink: that operation's request plus "op" naming it. Its schema: `rhiza describe apply --json`.

Arguments and flags:

- `<file>`: A JSON file of writes, or - for stdin (see the input schema); refs may name nodes added by earlier items (required)

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_set` (string): The change set written to (with --record, the new record change set)
- `drop` (array of string): Dry run only: the op IDs the entry would drop
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `entry` (string): The ops entry written; absent in a dry run
- `links` (array of string): The links the write created or retired, sorted
- `nodes` (array of string): The nodes the write created or changed, sorted; link endpoints are not included
- `ops` (array): Dry run only: the ops the entry would carry, as canonical op JSON
- `record` (boolean): True if the write opened and landed a record change set

## rhiza carve

Move nodes from one change set to another, keeping their IDs.

```
rhiza carve <nodes>... --from <from> --to <to> [--with-children]
```

Appends to the log.

Arguments and flags:

- `<nodes>`: The nodes to move, at least one: IDs, unique ID prefixes of 4+ characters, or handles, as the source sees them; each must be created in the source (required)
- `--from`: The change set to carve from: an ID or a unique prefix of 4+ characters (required)
- `--to`: The change set to carve into: an ID or a unique prefix of 4+ characters (required)
- `--with-children`: Also move every node created in the source below a named one, transitively

Output (`--json` fields):

- `depends_on` (string): The depends-on link added from the source to the target, if one was
- `dropped` (array of string): The op IDs dropped from the source, sorted
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `links` (array of string): The links moved, sorted
- `next` (string): A command that would help: withdrawing the source, when the carve left it with no ops
- `nodes` (array of string): The nodes moved, sorted
- `ops` (array of string): The new op IDs in the target, in order
- `source` (string): The change set carved from
- `source_entry` (string): The entry written to the source, dropping the moved ops; absent in a dry run
- `source_ops` (array): Dry run only: the ops the source's entry would carry, as canonical op JSON
- `target` (string): The change set carved into
- `target_entry` (string): The entry written to the target, re-creating them; absent in a dry run
- `target_ops` (array): Dry run only: the ops the target's entry would carry, as canonical op JSON

## rhiza change diff

Show a change set's changes: per node, each field before and after.

```
rhiza change diff [<ref>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<ref>`: The change set: a full ID or a unique prefix of 4+ characters; default --change, else the current one

Output (`--json` fields):

- `id` (string): The change set's ID
- `links` (array of object): The links it adds and retires, in change set order
- `nodes` (array of object): One entry per node the change set writes, in the order it first writes them

## rhiza change ls

List every change set with its kind, state and intent.

```
rhiza change ls
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_sets` (array of object): Every change set, sorted by ID
- `problems` (array of string): Everything wrong with the log and its change sets

## rhiza change new

Open a change set and make it current.

```
rhiza change new <intent> [--kind <kind>] [--source <source>]... [--title <title>] [--ref <ref>] [--workflow <workflow>]
```

Appends to the log.

Arguments and flags:

- `<intent>`: What the change set is for, in a sentence (required)
- `--kind`: intention (reviewed before it lands) or record (lands as is); default intention (one of intention, record)
- `--source`: A source node the change set comes from: an ID, ID prefix or handle (repeatable)
- `--title`: A short name for the change set, one line of at most 30 characters; default the intent's first clause
- `--ref`: An opaque external reference, such as an issue URL, at most 2048 bytes, trimmed; Rhiza never interprets it. An empty one means none
- `--workflow`: A workflow, by name, pinned to the change set: its ready pick is that workflow; default none (the dispatch rules choose)

Output (`--json` fields):

- `actor` (string): Who opened it; absent in a dry run before any actor is recorded
- `change_set` (string): The new change set's ID
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `entry` (string): The open entry's ID; absent in a dry run
- `intent` (string): The change set's intent
- `kind` (string): intention or record
- `ref` (string): The change set's opaque external reference, if any
- `sources` (array of string): The source node IDs, sorted
- `title` (string): The change set's title, else its intent's first clause
- `workflow` (string): The workflow pinned to the change set, if any

## rhiza change show

Show a change set: its intent, state, operations and decision.

```
rhiza change show [<ref>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<ref>`: The change set: a full ID or a unique prefix of 4+ characters; default --change, else the current one

Output (`--json` fields):

- `applied` (array of string): Every folded entry, in causal order
- `changes` (object): The change set's field-level diff, as change.diff reports it
- `current` (boolean): Whether it is the current change set
- `decided` (object): The applied accept or reject, if any
- `heads` (array of string): The entries a new entry would follow
- `history` (array of object): The lifecycle entries that applied, in causal order
- `id` (string): The change set's ID
- `intent` (string): The change set's intent
- `kind` (string): intention or record; empty without a valid open
- `leaves` (array of object): The live capabilities it adds that have no live child capability, in build order: each after every leaf it depends on, ties in tree order
- `notes` (array of object): The live notes that discuss it, oldest first
- `ops` (array): The current operations, as canonical op JSON, in change set order
- `problems` (array of string): Everything wrong with its entries
- `ref` (string): The change set's opaque external reference, if any: untrusted text
- `request_kind` (string): feature, bug or milestone: the kind of request that opened it, feature when none did; empty without a valid open
- `serves` (array of string): The intents its live serves links point to, in its write view, by link ID; empty when it serves none yet
- `sources` (array of string): The source node IDs
- `state` (string): The lifecycle state; empty without a valid open
- `superseded_by` (string): The change set that superseded it, if any
- `title` (string): The change set's title, else its intent's first clause
- `workflow` (string): The workflow its request named for its ready pick, if any

## rhiza change use

Set or clear the current change set.

```
rhiza change use [<ref>] [--none]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<ref>`: The change set: a full ID or a unique prefix of 4+ characters
- `--none`: Clear the current change set instead

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_set` (string): The current change set; absent when cleared
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if the current change set was left unchanged
- `intent` (string): Its intent

## rhiza check

Check the log, the links and the rendered markdown.

```
rhiza check [--base <base>] [--skip-reference]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--base`: The git revision the log may only have grown since; default the merge-base of HEAD with origin/HEAD, origin/main or main
- `--skip-reference`: Leave out the generated-reference comparison (docs/reference against rhiza docs) and the docs-command rule, which judge by this binary's registry; run code-check sets it, make self-check does not

Output (`--json` fields):

- `base` (string): The git revision the append-only rule compared against; empty when it was skipped
- `findings` (array of object): Every finding, sorted by rule (log, fold, model, in-flight, link, depends-on, evidence-actor, unclaimed, anchor, text-ref, dispatch, render, append-only), then path and IDs
- `merge_base_of` (string): The ref whose merge-base with HEAD is the default base; absent with --base
- `ok` (boolean): True when no finding fails
- `skipped` (string): Why the append-only rule was skipped, if it was

Exit code: set by the result, besides the shared codes.

## rhiza ci install

Install the Rhiza check as a GitHub workflow.

```
rhiza ci install [--force]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--force`: Overwrite an existing workflow that differs from the template

Output (`--json` fields):

- `unchanged` (array of string): The files that were already current
- `written` (array of string): The files written: new, or different from what was on disk

## rhiza daemon

Run the daemon in the foreground: one per repository, held by a lock in the git common dir.

```
rhiza daemon [--max-runs <max-runs>] [--once] [--autonomous] [--min-free <min-free>] [--permission-mode <permission-mode>] [--event-command <event-command>] [--notify-command <notify-command>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--max-runs`: Start runs until this many are running; default 2. An interrupted run takes no slot
- `--once`: Poll once, start what is picked and stop
- `--autonomous`: Start each run with --autonomous: it goes on without the owner
- `--min-free`: Start and resume nothing while the repo's filesystem has less free space than this: bytes, or a number with K, M, G or T (powers of 1024); default 10G; 0 turns the guard off
- `--permission-mode`: Start each run with this --permission-mode, for its agent steps that set none; checked against ship-change before the daemon starts
- `--event-command`: Run this command through sh -c in the repo root once per change set lifecycle move (proposed, accepted, rejected, withdrawn, superseded, landed, reopened) it has not handled, in log order, with the move as JSON on stdin and RHIZA_EVENT, RHIZA_EVENT_CHANGE, RHIZA_EVENT_ENTRY and RHIZA_EVENT_TITLE set; default: git config rhiza.eventCommand. The first run only records the moves already in the log. A failing or timed-out (10 s) command is logged and not retried
- `--notify-command`: Run this command through sh -c in the repo root once per new inbox item, with the item's JSON on stdin and RHIZA_INBOX_KIND, RHIZA_INBOX_ID, RHIZA_INBOX_CHANGE and RHIZA_INBOX_TITLE set; default: git config rhiza.notifyCommand. A failing or timed-out (10 s) command is logged and not retried

Output (`--json` fields):

- `planned` (array of string): The plan requests whose plan runs the daemon started, in order
- `process` (string): The daemon's process, as host:pid
- `resumed` (array of string): The interrupted runs the daemon resumed, in order
- `started` (array of string): The change sets whose runs the daemon started, in order

## rhiza daemon install

Run the root's daemon as a systemd user service: write and enable the unit and turn on lingering.

```
rhiza daemon install
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `path` (string): The unit file, absolute
- `unit` (string): The unit's name, such as rhiza-root.service
- `written` (boolean): Whether the unit file changed; false if it was already current

## rhiza daemon set

Validate and write one daemon setting to the repo's git config; a running daemon reads it at its next poll.

```
rhiza daemon set <key> <value> [--project <project>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<key>`: The setting: rhiza.daemon.paused, selfUpdate, maxRuns, minFree, permissionMode, usage.session, usage.weekly or usage.reserve, rhiza.daemon.watchdog.* or rhiza.project.watchdog.* (enabled, agentNudge, agentRetry, commandLimit, waitLimit, retryBudget, ciReruns, pollBehind, fileBugs, autonomousOnly), rhiza.web.host, rhiza.web.port, rhiza.ship.deployUrl, deployTimeout or ciWindow, or rhiza.autonomy.plan, accept, ship or signoff (required)
- `<value>`: The new value: true or false, a whole number, a token count, a percent, a size, a permission mode, an IP address, a port number or off, an http(s) URL, a duration, or auto or owner, as the key takes (required)
- `--project`: The registered project a project setting is written to; default the current project

Output (`--json` fields):

- `key` (string): The setting
- `scope` (string): Where it was written: machine (rhiza.toml) or project (git config)
- `value` (string): The value written

## rhiza daemon settings

List the daemon's settings, each with its value and where it comes from.

```
rhiza daemon settings [--project <project>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--project`: The registered project whose project settings to list; default the current project

Output (`--json` fields):

- `settings` (array of object): Every setting, in a fixed order

## rhiza daemon start

Start this repo's daemon: through its systemd unit when daemon install wrote one, else in the Rex tab 'rhiza daemon'.

```
rhiza daemon start
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `changed` (boolean): False when the daemon already ran and nothing was done
- `mode` (string): How this installation runs the daemon: service (a systemd user unit) or tab (the Rex tab 'rhiza daemon')

## rhiza daemon status

Show the daemon of this repository: whether it runs, its settings, its live runs and what it last started or resumed.

```
rhiza daemon status [--all] [--project <project>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--all`: Cover every registered project, from anywhere under a Rhiza root; the default at the root itself
- `--project`: Only this registered project's part of the daemon's state; default the current project, or every project at the root

Output (`--json` fields):

- `autonomous` (boolean): True when it starts each run with --autonomous
- `commit` (string): The git commit the daemon's binary was built from, as recorded when it started; absent when the build carried none
- `hooks` (array of object): The notify and event commands the daemon took at start, each with its source: daemon flag, git config or unset
- `last_poll` (string): When it last polled, RFC 3339 UTC
- `last_resumed` (object): The run it last resumed; absent if none
- `last_started` (object): The run it last started; absent if none
- `live` (integer): The machine-wide live runs holding a slot (running, not interrupted), summed over the daemon's projects
- `max` (integer): rhiza.daemon.maxRuns as the daemon's last poll recorded it: the cap live plus starting is counted against
- `max_runs` (integer): How many runs it keeps running at once
- `mode` (string): How this installation runs the daemon: service when daemon install wrote a systemd unit, else tab (the Rex tab 'rhiza daemon')
- `poll_behind` (string): Set while its last poll took longer than the watchdog's pollBehind multiple of the poll interval: how long it took and the limit; absent when polls keep up
- `process` (string): The daemon's process, as host:pid; absent when none ever ran
- `projects` (array of object): At the root or with --all: each registered, initialised project's runs, last start and resume, skips and unjournaled starts, in name order, the top-level runs, skipped and unjournaled then being empty; empty for one project
- `running` (boolean): True while a live daemon holds the repository's lock
- `runs` (array of object): The live runs (running or interrupted) as of its last poll
- `settings` (array of object): The settings as its last poll read them, each with its source: default, git config or flag
- `skipped` (array of object): The accepted change sets it did not start at its last poll, each with its reason
- `skipped_projects` (array of object): The registered projects the root daemon did not work at its last poll, each with its reason
- `started` (string): When the daemon started, RFC 3339 UTC
- `starting` (integer): The machine-wide starts and resumes not journaled yet, each holding a slot, summed over the daemon's projects, as of its last poll
- `stopped` (string): When the last daemon stopped, RFC 3339 UTC; absent while it runs
- `unjournaled` (array of object): The runs it started that never wrote a journal, by change set and when; it starts these again 15 minutes after the start, or sooner when a run of the change set journals
- `version` (string): The version of the binary the daemon runs, as recorded when it started
- `watchdog_actions` (array of string): The watchdog's last actions, newest first, each as its time and the log line: what it saw, what it did, the run or request; absent when it has done none
- `web` (string): The web UI as the daemon's last poll recorded it from rhiza.web.port: its URL (http://127.0.0.1:<port>), or off; it is the recorded setting, the listener is not probed; absent when none was recorded

## rhiza daemon stop

Stop this repo's daemon: through its systemd unit when daemon install wrote one, else by ending its process.

```
rhiza daemon stop
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `changed` (boolean): False when no daemon ran and nothing was done
- `mode` (string): How this installation runs the daemon: service (a systemd user unit) or tab (the Rex tab 'rhiza daemon')

## rhiza daemon uninstall

Stop, disable and remove the root's systemd user service.

```
rhiza daemon uninstall
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `path` (string): The unit file, absolute
- `removed` (boolean): Whether a unit file was removed; false if there was none
- `unit` (string): The unit's name, such as rhiza-root.service

## rhiza describe

Describe operations: their arguments and request and response schemas.

```
rhiza describe [<op>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<op>`: The operation to describe, such as change.new; every operation if empty

Output (`--json` fields):

- `operations` (array of object): The operations, sorted by name

## rhiza docs

Write the generated reference (CLI commands, settings, workflow file) under docs/reference.

```
rhiza docs [--out <out>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--out`: The folder to write into; default docs/reference in the project root, unless it holds files but none rhiza docs wrote

Output (`--json` fields):

- `unchanged` (integer): How many files were already current
- `written` (array of string): The files written: new, or different from what was on disk

## rhiza feed

List the change sets that landed, in land order, a page at a time.

```
rhiza feed [--limit <limit>] [--cursor <cursor>] [--since <since>] [--all] [--follow]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--limit`: The most change sets to return, 1 to 1000; default 100
- `--cursor`: Where to go on: the next_cursor of the page before
- `--since`: Keep the change sets landed at or after this time, RFC 3339
- `--all`: Include the change sets whose ops only create or update actor nodes, which are left out by default
- `--follow`: Stream each change set as it lands until interrupted: with neither cursor nor since only those landing after the start, else the backlog after that point first; one FeedItem per line with --json; limit then stops after that many, default unlimited

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_sets` (array of object): The landed change sets, oldest land first
- `next_cursor` (string): The cursor of the next page; absent when no more remain

## rhiza guide

Print the agent guide: the rhiza skill, the scrub skill, the plan skill or a topic.

```
rhiza guide [<name>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<name>`: The text to print: rhiza (the default), scrub, plan or a topic name; rhiza guide ls lists them

Output (`--json` fields):

- `name` (string): The text's name
- `text` (string): The text, as markdown
- `version` (string): The rhiza version the text ships in

## rhiza guide install

Install the agent guide into Claude Code as a skills-directory plugin.

```
rhiza guide install --agent <agent> [--project] [--force]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--agent`: The agent to install the guide for: claude (Claude Code) (required; one of claude)
- `--project`: Install into this repository's .claude/skills/ instead of ~/.claude/skills/
- `--force`: Overwrite a folder rhiza guide install did not write; other files in it are kept

Output (`--json` fields):

- `dir` (string): The plugin folder, absolute
- `unchanged` (array of string): The files that were already current
- `written` (array of string): The files written: new, or different from what was on disk

## rhiza guide ls

List the guide's skills and topics with their sizes.

```
rhiza guide ls
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `texts` (array of object): The texts: the rhiza, scrub and plan skills, then the topics by name

## rhiza health

Report the daemon, autonomy settings, the machine trust, free disk, the usage hold, the main checkout, CI stability, inbox, queued requests, roadmap and rhiza check, each part ok, warn or bad; exit 1 when any part is bad.

```
rhiza health [--all] [--project <project>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--all`: Cover every registered project, from anywhere under a Rhiza root; the default at the root itself
- `--project`: Only this registered project's parts; default the current project, or every project at the root

Output (`--json` fields):

- `parts` (array of object): Every part, in a fixed order: daemon, autonomy, machine, disk, usage, then main, ci, schedules (only for a project with schedules), inbox, requests, roadmap and check, once for the project or, over every project, once for each in name order tagged with its project
- `state` (string): The worst state of any part

Exit code: set by the result, besides the shared codes.

## rhiza hook ls

List the notify and event hook commands, each with its command and source: daemon flag (from a live daemon), git config or unset.

```
rhiza hook ls
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `hooks` (array of object): The notify hook, then the event hook

## rhiza hook run

Run the notify or event hook command once with a sample payload, showing its output and exit status; writes nothing.

```
rhiza hook run <hook> [--command <command>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<hook>`: The hook to run: notify or event (required)
- `--command`: Run this command instead of the hook's own, through sh -c in the repo root

Output (`--json` fields):

- `code` (integer): The command's exit code: 0 when it succeeded, else non-zero (1 when it timed out or did not start)
- `command` (string): The command that ran
- `error` (string): Why it failed; absent on success
- `hook` (string): The hook that ran
- `output` (string): What the command wrote to stdout and stderr
- `payload` (string): The sample JSON sent on stdin
- `source` (string): Where the command is set: command flag, daemon flag or git config

Exit code: set by the result, besides the shared codes.

## rhiza inbox

List what waits on the owner across every run: questions, sign-offs, failed runs, runs the daemon gave up on, interrupted runs it skipped because their change set is no longer accepted, stalled sessions of live runs and sessions of live runs blocked on a permission prompt, and the daemon's low disk space, oldest first.

```
rhiza inbox [--project <project>] [--all]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--project`: Only this registered project's inbox; default the current project, or every project at the root
- `--all`: Every registered project's inbox, from anywhere under the root

Output (`--json` fields):

- `items` (array of object): The items waiting on the owner, oldest first; empty when none

## rhiza inbox approve

Approve the sign-off an inbox item waits at, as run approve does on that item's run; exit 2 on any other kind of item.

```
rhiza inbox approve <item> [--foreground] [--project <project>] [--all]
```

Appends to the log.

Arguments and flags:

- `<item>`: The inbox item: its short ID from rhiza inbox, or a unique prefix of it; it must be a sign-off (required)
- `--foreground`: Drive the run in this process, rather than hand it to the daemon. The daemon passes it to the detached process it starts
- `--project`: Only look in this registered project; default the current project, or every project at the root
- `--all`: Look in every registered project, from anywhere under the root

Output (`--json` fields):

- `changes` (string): With changes: the checks step that fixes them
- `daemon` (string): With queued: the daemon's process, as host:pid; empty when no daemon runs and the run waits for one
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was journalled or run
- `queued` (boolean): True when the sign-off was journalled and the run's continuation queued for the daemon, which drives it headless, rather than driven in this process; absent otherwise
- `run` (object): The run after it was continued; in a dry run, or when queued, as it stands. The command exits 1 when the run failed
- `signoff` (object): The sign-off journalled, or in a dry run the one that would be

Exit code: set by the result, besides the shared codes.

## rhiza inbox open

Focus the Rex tab an inbox item waits in: the asking session's for a question, the run's journalled tab for the rest.

```
rhiza inbox open <item> [--project <project>] [--all]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<item>`: The inbox item: its short ID from rhiza inbox, or a unique prefix of it (required)
- `--project`: Only look in this registered project; default the current project, or every project at the root
- `--all`: Look in every registered project, from anywhere under the root

Output (`--json` fields):

- `item` (string): The item's short ID
- `kind` (string): question, signoff, failed, gave-up or skipped
- `opened` (boolean): True when the tab was focused
- `run` (string): The run it belongs to
- `tab` (string): The Rex block of the tab, when one is recorded
- `tab_gone` (boolean): True when the tab is no longer in Rex, or none was recorded

## rhiza inbox request-changes

Ask for changes to the sign-off an inbox item waits at, as run request-changes does on that item's run; exit 2 on any other kind of item.

```
rhiza inbox request-changes <item> <file> [--foreground] [--project <project>] [--all]
```

Appends to the log.

Input: {"findings":[{"check":...,"severity":...,"leaf":...,"place":...,"reason":...},...]}, at least one; see rhiza describe run.request-changes. Its schema: `rhiza describe inbox.request-changes --json`.

Arguments and flags:

- `<item>`: The inbox item: its short ID from rhiza inbox, or a unique prefix of it; it must be a sign-off (required)
- `<file>`: A JSON file of the owner's findings, or - for stdin (see the input schema) (required)
- `--foreground`: Drive the run in this process, rather than hand it to the daemon. The daemon passes it to the detached process it starts
- `--project`: Only look in this registered project; default the current project, or every project at the root
- `--all`: Look in every registered project, from anywhere under the root

Output (`--json` fields):

- `changes` (string): With changes: the checks step that fixes them
- `daemon` (string): With queued: the daemon's process, as host:pid; empty when no daemon runs and the run waits for one
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was journalled or run
- `queued` (boolean): True when the sign-off was journalled and the run's continuation queued for the daemon, which drives it headless, rather than driven in this process; absent otherwise
- `run` (object): The run after it was continued; in a dry run, or when queued, as it stands. The command exits 1 when the run failed
- `signoff` (object): The sign-off journalled, or in a dry run the one that would be

Exit code: set by the result, besides the shared codes.

## rhiza init

Create a Rhiza repository in the current folder.

```
rhiza init
```

Output (`--json` fields):

- `repo` (string): The new repository's ID
- `root` (string): The absolute path of the project root holding .rhiza

## rhiza land

Land the change set: an accepted intention, or a record.

```
rhiza land
```

Appends to the log.

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_set` (string): The change set moved
- `cleared_current` (boolean): True if the move ended the current change set and cleared it
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `entry` (string): The entry written; absent in a dry run
- `from` (string): The state before the move
- `reason` (string): The reason of an accept or reject
- `rule` (string): The rule of an accept or reject
- `to` (string): The state after the move

## rhiza link

Link two nodes, two change sets, or one of each.

```
rhiza link <from> <type> <to> [--note <note>] [--decision <decision>]
```

Appends to the log.

Arguments and flags:

- `<from>`: The node or change set the link starts at: an ID, a unique ID prefix of 4+ characters, or a live node's handle (required)
- `<type>`: What the link says (required; one of serves, constrains, exempts, depends-on, relates-to, decided-by, answers, blocks, supersedes, derived-from, discovered-from, implements, verifies, observes, discusses)
- `<to>`: The node or change set the link ends at (required)
- `--note`: Why; required on relates-to and exempts
- `--decision`: The decision node behind an exempts link (exempts only, required there)

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_set` (string): The change set written to (with --record, the new record change set)
- `drop` (array of string): Dry run only: the op IDs the entry would drop
- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `entry` (string): The ops entry written; absent in a dry run
- `links` (array of string): The links the write created or retired, sorted
- `nodes` (array of string): The nodes the write created or changed, sorted; link endpoints are not included
- `ops` (array): Dry run only: the ops the entry would carry, as canonical op JSON
- `record` (boolean): True if the write opened and landed a record change set

## rhiza log

List every change set that touched a node or link, in order.

```
rhiza log <ref> [--view <view>] [--limit <limit>] [--cursor <cursor>] [--all]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<ref>`: The node or link: an ID, a unique ID prefix of 4+ characters, or a node's handle (required)
- `--view`: as-is, to-be or what-if:<change set>; default what-if of a draft or proposed effective change set, to-be of an accepted one, else as-is
- `--limit`: The most change sets to return, 1 to 1000; default 100
- `--cursor`: Where to go on: the next_cursor of the page before
- `--all`: Return every change set, ignoring --limit and --cursor

Output (`--json` fields):

- `change_sets` (array of object): The change sets that touched it, in apply order; one page
- `next_cursor` (string): The cursor of the next page; absent when no more remain
- `target` (object): The node or link
- `view` (string): The view read

## rhiza ls

List nodes, filtered by kind and parent, a page at a time.

```
rhiza ls [--kind <kind>]... [--parent <parent>] [--retired] [--limit <limit>] [--cursor <cursor>] [--view <view>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `--kind`: Keep the nodes of this kind; repeat for several; default every kind (repeatable; one of intent, capability, constraint, decision, question, evidence, source, actor, anchor, note)
- `--parent`: Keep the nodes directly under this node: an ID, a unique ID prefix of 4+ characters, or a live node's handle
- `--retired`: Keep retired nodes too
- `--limit`: The most nodes to return, 1 to 1000; default 100
- `--cursor`: Where to go on: the next_cursor of the page before
- `--view`: as-is, to-be or what-if:<change set>; default follows the effective change set

Output (`--json` fields):

- `next_cursor` (string): The cursor of the next page; absent when no more remain
- `nodes` (array of object): The nodes, sorted by ID
- `view` (string): The view it was read in: as-is, to-be or what-if:<change set ID>

## rhiza mv

## rhiza question answer

Answer an open question that blocks a change set: write the owner's words as a Decision quoting them, linked answers to the question, into --change.

Appends to the log.

- `change_set` (string): The change set written to (with --record, the new record change set)

- `entry` (string): The ops entry written; absent in a dry run
- `links` (array of string): The links the write created or retired, sorted

- `ops` (array): Dry run only: the ops the entry would carry, as canonical op JSON
- `record` (boolean): True if the write opened and landed a record change set

## rhiza request

Queue a plan request in this clone: the daemon starts a plan run for it.

```
rhiza request <text> [--kind <kind>] [--milestone <milestone>] [--workflow <workflow>] [--ref <ref>]
```

Arguments and flags:

- `<text>`: What to plan, in one line (required)
- `--kind`: feature, bug or milestone; default feature. A bug's plan run opens its change set with the intent prefixed 'Fix ' (so its title names the bug), a milestone's a record change set (one of feature, bug, milestone)
- `--milestone`: A milestone intent, by handle or ID, the request's plan should serve; default none (the planner serves the open milestone it fits)
- `--workflow`: A workflow, by name, for the change set the request's plan run opens: it overrides that change set's ready pick only, not the plan run's own workflow; default none (the dispatch rules choose)
- `--ref`: An opaque external reference, such as an issue URL, at most 2048 bytes, trimmed; Rhiza never interprets it. An empty one means none

Output (`--json` fields):

- `dry_run` (boolean): True if nothing was written
- `note` (string): A one-line risk note, only for a request with a --ref while the request-exposed list is not empty: it names the flagged workflows and says outside text reaches agents with no permission checks; never changes the outcome
- `request` (object): The request
